fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (50%, $272 = FY2027 consensus EPS $4.93 x 55x), EV/sales on 2028E revenue (30%, $258 = $9.0B x 9x + ~$2.45B equity-adjusted net cash, / 323M diluted shares) and a DCF (20%, $158, now including net cash). Blended fair value ~$245, about 15% below the $288.70 close.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY2027 non-GAAP EPS $4.93 (Alpha Vantage consensus, 28 analysts, range $2.95-$7.01; up from $4.36 90 days ago) x 55x. That is ~39x my own FY2028 EPS extrapolation of ~$7.00 (+40%; there is no FY28 consensus), which is what the market will price in Sep 2027. Premium to electrical-equipment peers for 40%+ growth, well below today's ~77x NTM P/E. Unchanged from round 1; net cash is already reflected in EPS via interest income.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: 2028E revenue $9.0B (FY2027 consensus $6.79B +33%, my extrapolation) x 9x EV/sales = $81B EV, plus ~$2.45B equity-adjusted net cash ($2.67B cash at 6/30/26 less ~$0.2B financing obligations; the $2.475B of 0% 2030 converts are in the money at ~$194.97 conversion and their ~12.6M shares are already in the 323.3M diluted count, so they are treated as equity), / 323M diluted shares = ~$258.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Valued as of Sep 2027. Revenue $4.05B (2026) growing 60%/40%/30%/25%/20% to ~$17.7B in 2031. Terminal FCF margin 18%, WACC 10%, terminal growth 5%. Terminal value ~$67B discounted to ~$43B, plus ~$5.5B PV of interim FCF = ~$48.5B EV, plus ~$2.45B net cash = ~$51B equity / 323M shares = ~$158. Very sensitive: 15% margin, 11% WACC, 4% growth gives ~$100.

bear.story: AI data-center capex digestion plus Project Jupiter slipping hard: the NM air-quality permit is not decided by the Nov 23, 2026 deadline (hearing officer still unappointed after the NM Supreme Court stay was lifted Sep 17) and/or the Green Chile pipeline misses ~Feb 1, 2027, deferring a large slice of 2027-28 shipments. FY2027 guide (Feb 2027) comes in well below ~$6.8B revenue, EPS ~$3.5-4.0, and the multiple compresses to ~30-35x as the S&P-inclusion bid fades. Scandium/China litigation overhang. ~$7.5/share of net cash cushions slightly vs round 1.

base.story: Fremont reaches 2 GW by end-2026. FY2026 lands ~$4.1B revenue / ~$2.7 EPS; FY2027 ~$6.5-7B / ~$5 EPS, with 2028 visibility near $7 (my extrapolation). Jupiter is a timing issue only: Oracle's force majeure is a lease-payment deferral right toward developer Blue Owl, not a termination, and more than half of the >= $8B equipment backlog (Morgan Stanley est.) is non-Oracle. Multiple compresses from ~77x NTM to ~40-45x forward, roughly offsetting earnings growth, so the stock ends near spot.

bull.story: Jupiter permit granted on time, more direct hyperscaler deals beyond Oracle, capacity stepping to 3-4 GW and margin mix-up drive 2027 EPS above $6.5 and 2028 viewed at $9-10. The market keeps a 50x+ multiple for a scarce on-site AI power provider (sell-side targets already moving up: Mizuho $351, Clear Street $330, UBS $325).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$150 (about -48%, under the ~$164 post-Q2 level of late July) BE would trade at ~30x FY2027 consensus EPS of $4.93, which only makes sense with deep estimate cuts: Jupiter actually cancelled or pushed beyond 2028 (permit denied or pipeline far past Feb 2027 with no redeployment of units), a Feb 2027 FY27 guide well below ~$6.8B revenue, gross margin back under ~30%, or a real scandium supply disruption. The 112% realized vol makes 30-40% drawdowns routine (it fell ~28% from $351 to ~$253 in Aug-Sep without fundamental change), so moves to $170-230 are noise.

reasoning: Round 2. Bloom Energy is at $288.70 after a +317% year on an AI on-site-power inflection: 2Q26 revenue $1.065B (+166%), non-GAAP GM 34.3%, EPS $0.78, OCF +$226M, FY26 guide raised to $3.9-4.2B / $2.55-2.85 EPS; FY2027 consensus $6.79B / $4.93 EPS (rising). The supervisor showed my round-1 ~$1.5B net cash was unsupported: cash was $2.67B at 6/30/26 and the $2.475B of 0% 2030 converts (issued Oct 2025, conversion ~$194.97) are in the money and already in the 323.3M diluted count, so equity-adjusted net cash is ~$2.45B. I accept that; it lifts EV/sales to ~$258 (+$3) and, because my round-1 DCF equity value had effectively omitted cash, lifts the DCF to ~$158 (+$8). P/E is unchanged. Blended fair value rises from $243 to ~$245. On Jupiter I verified: Oracle's Sep 24 notice went to developer Blue Owl as a lease-deferral right; Oracle and Blue Owl reaffirmed and Bloom says the 2.4 GW contract stands; the NM Supreme Court lifted its stay Sep 17, but NMED has not appointed a hearing officer and the permit deadline is Nov 23; Morgan Stanley (Overweight, $310) estimates >= $8B equipment backlog, more than half non-Oracle, and notes Jupiter is outside 2026 guidance. I folded the permit/pipeline risk into the bear case instead of giving it a separate scenario, because it is mainly a timing risk to 2027-28 revenue and not a backlog loss, and I trimmed the bear weight from 25% to 23% and raised the bear price to $135 (net cash). Scenario mean ~$305 (0.23x135 + 0.52x295 + 0.25x480). I move my median from $275 to ~$282, still below spot because my fundamental value ($245) is below spot and multiple compression from ~59x FY27 EPS absorbs most 2028 growth. Distribution: lognormal-ish around $282 with sigma ~0.75 (below the 112% realized vol but far above the large-cap ±25-35% base rate), with slightly fatter left tail at the lowest strikes. P(>= spot) ~0.485, P(>= $144) ~0.815, P(>= $577, 2x) ~0.165. Research used ~5 extra searches in round 2.
